title: Habsburg monarchy under Charles V
summary: Through a chain of inheritances, Charles of Habsburg became king of Castile and Aragon in 1516 and, in 1519, ruler of the Austrian lands and Holy Roman Emperor, holding one of the largest collections of territories in European history. His reign saw Spain conquer the Aztec and Inca realms, and constant wars with France, with the Ottomans under Suleiman and against the spread of Protestantism. When he abdicated in 1556, the Habsburgs divided into a Spanish and an Austrian line.

uncertainty.note: Reign spans his election as Holy Roman Emperor in 1519 through his series of formal abdications in 1555–1556.

as_recorded.value: reigned from 1519 until his abdication in 1556
Charles finally laid down his office in 1556, abdicating from the Spanish throne in favour of his son Philip

importance.justification: Joined Spain, its American empire, the Netherlands, Italy and the Empire under one ruler and left the Spanish-Austrian division of the Habsburgs (R3 D2 T3 L3).

sources.title: Charles V and the empire ‘on which the sun never set’
